title: All creation (Psalm 103 [104])
hookLine: springs, cedars, wild goats, the sea full of creatures

cards: Put on a nature documentary. Mountain goats balanced on an impossible cliff. A whale surfacing, enormous and unhurried.
Lions at dusk. A spring bubbling out of a rock, and birds lining up to drink. The narrator's voice goes quiet with wonder.
Long before cameras, someone made the same film in words: a psalm that walks through the whole created world, one creature at a time.

teach.b: Psalm 103 in the Douay, 104 in most Bibles, opens with the same line as the psalm before it: bless the Lord, O my soul. This time the reason isn't mercy. It's the world.
God is clothed with light as with a garment, stretching out the sky like a tent. Then the tour. Springs run down between the hills, and wild asses come to drink.
Birds nest by the water and sing among the branches.
Grass for the cattle, and for people, three gifts: "wine may cheer the heart of man," oil to make the face shine, and bread to strengthen the heart.
The cedars of Lebanon, planted by God, with sparrows nesting there and the heron's house in the highest of them.
Then a line the Douay makes delightful: "The highest mountains are a refuge for the harts, the rock for the irchins." Irchins are hedgehogs.
The Hebrew seems to mean a small rock animal, the hyrax, but the Latin chose hedgehogs, so the Douay gave God's rocks to the hedgehogs.
The moon marks the seasons, lions roar for their prey at night, and people go out to work until evening.

teach.h: A SEA CREATURE MADE TO PLAY.
teach.b: Then the sea, with creatures without number, ships sailing across it, and the great sea creature, in the Douay a sea dragon, made "to play therein."
At the summit: "How great are thy works, O Lord? thou hast made all things in wisdom." Everything waits on God for food; when God takes away their breath, they die.
And then the line the Church sings at Pentecost: "Thou shalt send forth thy spirit, and they shall be created: and thou shalt renew the face of the earth."

how: Catholics sing Psalm 103 [104] as the responsorial psalm at Pentecost, with its line about sending forth the Spirit to renew the face of the earth, and at the Easter Vigil after the creation reading.

o: everything God made, from springs to the sea
only the living animals, not the land or sea
the kings who ruled Israel, one by one

games.q: what's inside the psalm — tap the pairs.
p: to cheer the heart of man

s: in the Douay, the rocks are a refuge for hedgehogs
the high hills are a refuge for the harts, the rock for the irchins.
the psalm treats the great sea creature as God's enemy
it says God formed it to play in the sea.
the psalm says bread, wine and oil are gifts for people
wine to cheer the heart, oil to make the face shine, bread to strengthen.

games.q: the psalm has walked through springs, birds, cedars, goats, lions and the sea. what does it say at the top of the list?
o: how great are thy works, O Lord: thou hast made all things in wisdom.
the world is a dangerous place.
games.why: how great are thy works, O Lord? thou hast made all things in wisdom. the tour ends in wonder, and then in the Spirit renewing the earth.

practice: Step outside if you can, or look out a window, and like the psalm, make a slow list: a tree, a bird, a cloud, a dog walking its person, weeds in a crack in the sidewalk. Name each one quietly, and give it a breath before the next.
If you pray, end with the psalm's line, how great are thy works, O Lord; if you don't, let the list be its own kind of wonder.

wordCard.voice: All creation. The psalm's tour of the world, from springs and cedars to hedgehogs and the sea, all made in wisdom. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: how many (or how great) are your works.

carryVoice: Your line: how great are thy works. Even the hedgehogs got a rock. That's day one hundred seventy-eight.
